text: APDS 1.0.0Read the overviewOverviewChapters and rulesNormative semanticsJSON Schema (canonical $id)Conformance fixtures and instructionsAuthoritative GitHub source · apds-v1.0.0AgentPM APDS 1.0.0 Agent Package Definition Standard Identifier: agentpm · Version: 1.0.0 · Status: normative specification AgentPM's Agent Package Definition Standard (APDS) 1.0.0 defines how Agent Packages and their reusable Components are described, composed and interpreted. An Agent Package is a complete, authored Agent system. It can combine Tools, Skills, Knowledge, Memory Blueprints, Instruction Profiles and a Loop in one reusable definition. For example, a document-review Agent Package might combine a Skill containing review instructions, a Knowledge package with reference material and a Loop defining the review workflow. APDS 1.0.0 defines how those pieces relate across compatible Runners. APDS 1.0.0 gives developers a common contract for building, validating and running compatible Agent Packages without requiring a particular Registry, framework or Runner. A structural pass alone does not establish full conformance to APDS 1.0.0. The schema, semantic rules and applicable conformance expectations together define this version. Documents and precedence DocumentRolemanifest.schema.jsonDefines valid manifest structuresemantics.mdDefines what declarations mean and how they must be interpretedconformance/rule-index.mdLocates semantic rules by subject and evaluation scopeconformance/semantic-cases.mdIllustrates composition and Runner interpretation expectationsconformance/README.mdExplains validation and conformance testsconformance/fixture-index.jsonSupplies validation inputs, context and expected resultsconformance/runner-observations.jsonSupplies separate Manager/Runner behavior scenariosconformance/fixtures/valid/Expected structurally valid manifests for all eight kindsconformance/structural-cases.jsonExpected acceptance and rejection of description edge caseschecksums.jsonIdentifies the versioned files and their checksums The schema and semantic rules apply together. Fixtures illustrate expected outcomes; they do not override either document. Resolve conflicts explicitly before release. Examples and implementation guidance do not introduce additional normative requirements. To start implementing structural validation: Obtain the versioned schema from this bundle and retain a trusted local copy. Validate manifests with a JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 validator using that copy. Check that the nine valid fixtures pass, including the minimal Agent with no Components. Apply the description cases in structural-cases.json and compare results with each case's expected outcome. Then follow the conformance quickstart and use semantics.md with the shared fixture index for checks beyond structure. Terminology and roles TermManifest kindMeaningAgent PackageagentA versioned, authored Agent systemComponent—An independently reusable artifact that an Agent Package can composeTooltoolAn executable capability with declared inputs and outputsSkillskillProcedural know-how for a task, with optional Tool dependenciesKnowledgeknowledgeAuthored context or prepared retrieval data for an AgentMemory BlueprintmemoryA declaration of durable memory structures, record formats, policies and operationsInstruction ProfileprofileReusable identity, behavioral guidance, communication style and constraintsLooploopA declarative workflow of phases, outcomes and transitionsTemplatetemplateA scaffold for creating a project or workspaceManager—Software that discovers, installs and manages packages and their dependenciesRegistry—A service that distributes package versions and associated metadataRunner—Software that interprets supported declarations and executes an Agent or capability Authors produce declarations. Validators evaluate the supplied manifest, composition or content. Managers, Registries and Runners may perform validation in their own workflows, but their roles and the evidence available to them differ. Artifact kinds and names All eight artifact kinds use agent.json. Only agent is an Agent Package. The six Component kinds remain independently usable; Templates remain scaffolds. The top-level name is local and unscoped, such as document-reviewer. Dependency references use namespaced identities, such as @example/search. An Agent Package may omit all Components. Conformance does not establish whether a particular Runner can execute it. Declaring the standard A producer declares the intended contract through standard: { "kind": "agent", "name": "document-reviewer", "version": "1.0.0", "description": "Review documents and explain proposed changes.", "standard": { "id": "agentpm", "version": "1.0.0" } } The top-level version identifies the artifact version. standard.id and standard.version select the APDS 1.0.0 contract. An optional $schema URI helps editors locate the structural schema; it is not a standard declaration and cannot override standard. A declaration is also not proof that anyone validated the package. Compatibility handling for older manifests without standard belongs to implementations, not to a second APDS authoring format. Evaluation levels and evidence Standalone (intrinsic) validation: check the supplied manifest's structure and local relationships without resolving external dependencies. Resolved-composition validation: check relationships against the actual selected dependency manifests. Packaged-content validation: check supplied referenced files and their declared relationships. Runner and environment: check supported capabilities, runtime availability, credentials and local readiness. These checks are not conformance to APDS 1.0.0. When dependencies or packaged files aren't available for inspection, the corresponding checks remain unevaluated. Missing required content from an otherwise complete artifact may be a conformance violation. Report what was checked and what remains unknown. Signing, scanning, Runner compatibility and readiness require separate evidence. Registry and Runner independence APDS 1.0.0 is independent of a particular Registry, Manager or Runner. Implementers can consume the contract and fixtures without using AgentPM's CLI, service, lockfile or built-in Runner. A Registry can validate a package without executing it; a Runner can interpret a supported package obtained through another distribution mechanism. Boundaries and implementation support APDS 1.0.0 does not choose a model provider, prompt format, storage backend, approval interface, deployment platform or orchestration framework. It does not require a Registry to run Tools, Loops or Memory operations during validation. An implementation claiming support for APDS 1.0.0 should identify this version, its role, the evaluation levels it provides and any unsupported capabilities. It must not present proprietary checks or a replacement schema as proof of conformance to APDS 1.0.0. The semantic contract specifies portable interpretation; implementation strategies remain separate. Version 1.0.0 immutability and extensions Once published, the APDS 1.0.0 schema, semantic rules and normative expected fixture outcomes are immutable. Do not move its release tag or replace its bytes. Any normative-file change requires a new standard version: a major version for incompatible validity or meaning changes, a minor version for compatible additions, and a patch version for corrections preserving validity and meaning. Even editorial corrections receive new published bytes under a new version. Objects stay closed wherever the schema declares additionalProperties: false. Unknown root keys are errors, not implicit extensions. Adding a field to a released contract requires a new standard version and an explicit compatibility decision. Existing open data surfaces, such as Tool input/output JSON Schemas, do not open unrelated manifest objects. Canonical source and editor links The canonical source is this versioned directory in the agentpm-dev/cli repository. AgentPM's compatibility/editor path, schemas/agentpm.manifest.schema.json, mirrors this schema. That convenience path is not a separate authority or an APDS requirement. The schema's version-stable $id, also suitable for an editor $schema, is: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentpm-dev/cli/refs/tags/apds-v1.0.0/standards/agentpm/1.0.0/manifest.schema.json Validators should use a trusted bundled copy of their supported contract, without fetching a mutable repository branch during routine validation. Development checks against other schemas cannot establish conformance to APDS 1.0.0. The release tag apds-v1.0.0 identifies this versioned bundle. Reporting ambiguity Report ambiguities through the CLI repository's issue tracker. Identify APDS 1.0.0 and include the relevant schema path or semantic rule, a minimal manifest or composition, and the expected versus observed interpretation. Include the implementation/version when its behavior exposed the ambiguity. Handle corrections under the versioning policy; an ambiguity report does not change this version's meaning.Chapters and rulesThe text below reproduces the published semantics. Conformance, interpretation and compatibilityRule linksAPDS-CONF-001APDS-CONF-002APDS-CONF-003APDS-CONF-004APDS-CONF-005AgentPM APDS 1.0.0 semantics Identifier: agentpm · Version: 1.0.0 · Status: normative specification This document defines what APDS 1.0.0 declarations mean. Start with the README for the artifact kinds and roles; use the schema for exact field shapes. The rule index lists each rule's subjects, evaluation scopes and related semantic cases. The fixture index supplies validation inputs and expected outcomes; Runner observations describe separate behavior checks. Follow the conformance quickstart to use them with an implementation. 1. Scope, roles and normative language An author defines an artifact. A validator checks supplied declarations, dependencies or files. A Manager selects and manages artifacts. A Registry distributes them. A Runner interprets supported declarations during execution. One implementation can perform several roles. MUST and MUST NOT express requirements. SHOULD and SHOULD NOT express recommendations whose departure needs a considered reason. MAY expresses a permitted choice. Lowercase uses have their ordinary meaning. Examples and explanations clarify rules; they add no requirements. APDS-SCOPE-001 Role-specific support. An implementation MUST preserve the rules applicable to the roles and constructs it claims to support. A Registry acting as a validator has validator responsibilities; it need not execute a Runner. Supporting one optional capability does not require implementing unrelated capabilities. APDS-SCOPE-002 One versioned contract. Authors and validators MUST apply the schema and these semantic rules together for APDS 1.0.0. Normative fixture expectations MUST agree with both. A fixture cannot override a rule. The published normative files and rule meanings MUST remain immutable under this version; changes follow the versioning policy. Model/provider selection, prompt assembly, approval interfaces, hooks, storage engines, retrieval algorithms, schedulers, internal retries and trace formats remain implementation choices except where a rule below defines an observable authored guarantee. Unsupported execution constructs affect Runner compatibility, not the validity of an otherwise conformant artifact. 2. Artifact identity, versions, namespaces and references An artifact has its own kind, local name and version. A dependency reference identifies another artifact through a namespace and, optionally, a version selector. These are different identities used for different purposes. APDS-ID-001 Explicit standard. An author claiming APDS 1.0.0 MUST declare standard: { "id": "agentpm", "version": "1.0.0" }. The optional editor $schema neither substitutes for that declaration nor selects different semantics. A validator MUST NOT silently substitute a supported version for an unsupported declaration. Historical compatibility handling is outside this normative authoring format. APDS-ID-002 Artifact identity and purpose. Authors MUST preserve the schema's distinction between local name, artifact version and declared standard version. A distribution namespace qualifies a reference, not the local manifest name. The root description MUST contain non-whitespace text as defined by the schema's explicit Unicode White_Space class. kind: "agent" identifies an Agent Package; template identifies a scaffold. The six other kinds identify Components. APDS-ID-003 Reference forms. Authors MUST use the schema's package-reference forms: a namespaced string with an optional numeric version selector, or an object containing name and optional version. A two-component selector such as 1.2 selects that major/minor line; a complete version selects that version. Omission leaves the version unconstrained. Literal latest, *, caret, tilde and comparison-range syntax are not additional APDS 1.0.0 manifest forms. The field containing a reference determines its required artifact kind. APDS-ID-004 Content paths. A path declared as artifact-relative MUST identify content inside its containing artifact using the schema's relative-path syntax. Implementations reading supplied content MUST reject an escape from that boundary, including an escape through a resolved link. Consumer-owned context paths are relative to the consuming project instead; they are not paths into a dependency package. Missing inspection context is handled by APDS-CONF-002. 3. Dependencies and composition A dependency states what the artifact relies on. A binding states where a declared Component participates. Installing or resolving a dependency does not itself bind it or invoke it. APDS-GRAPH-001 Allowed relationships. Dependencies MUST follow their kind-specific schema. An Agent may declare any of the six Component families, including a single Loop. A Skill may declare Tools. A Template's dependency groups may declare Agents and Components. Knowledge, Memory, Profile and Loop artifacts have no package dependency declarations. The top-level profile object is Profile metadata; Agent Profile dependencies use plural profiles. An Agent Package MAY omit all dependencies, bindings and its Loop. A validator MUST NOT require them merely because a particular Runner needs them to execute an Agent. APDS-GRAPH-002 Selected versions. A Manager supplying a resolved composition MUST identify the selected artifact versions and preserve each declaring artifact's dependency edges and constraints. References MUST resolve to the intended kind, namespace, name and selected version in their owning composition, not an arbitrary installed artifact with the same name. An unavailable graph leaves dependent checks unevaluated; a supplied graph selecting an incompatible kind or version establishes a violation. No particular resolver, lockfile, integrity algorithm or installation layout is required. Different versions may occur in different dependency contexts; they are not interchangeable capabilities. APDS-GRAPH-003 Unambiguous references. An author MUST NOT declare duplicate identities within one dependency collection, including equivalent string/object references. Versionless bindings MUST resolve unambiguously through the containing Agent's selected composition. A Manager or Runner MUST NOT conceal a version ambiguity by merging distinct selected artifacts. Direct and transitive paths remain distinguishable even when they reach the same artifact. 4. Agent bindings and effective capabilities Global bindings apply throughout a run. Phase bindings add declarations for their named phase. The active Loop can restrict which resulting capabilities may be used. APDS-BIND-001 Declared membership. Each explicit Tool, Skill, Knowledge, Memory or Profile binding MUST name an Agent dependency from the matching top-level collection. Bindings use versionless package identities; they do not introduce dependencies. Memory selectors MUST identify spaces or operations in the selected Blueprint when that Blueprint is available for inspection. Inherited Skill Tools follow APDS-SKILL-002, without requiring duplicate Agent Tool declarations. APDS-BIND-002 Phase names. An Agent with phase bindings MUST declare a Loop dependency. Every binding phase MUST exist in that resolved Loop. Absence of the dependency declaration is a standalone defect; an unknown phase in a supplied Loop is a resolved-composition defect. A validator without the Loop cannot claim to have checked its phase names. APDS-BIND-003 Additive scopes. A Runner MUST combine applicable global and active-phase bindings. A phase binding MUST NOT replace or remove a global binding. For the same Memory Blueprint, applicable space and operation selectors combine by set union. Other phases receive only their own phase bindings plus global bindings and independently applicable inheritance. APDS-BIND-004 Eligibility is not invocation. Applicable bindings and inherited capabilities are candidates subject to Loop access rules, execution authorization and runtime support. A Runner MUST NOT treat a binding as automatic invocation or permission to bypass those restrictions. It MUST distinguish an unavailable implementation or environment from an invalid declaration. APDS-BIND-005 MCP and consumer context. Each bindings.mcp entry MUST have a unique ID and select Tool identities declared by the Agent. It identifies a named Model Context Protocol (MCP) Tool surface; it does not authorize unrelated capabilities or bypass Loop Tool restrictions. A Runner interpreting imported or exposed Tools MUST preserve those restrictions. Connection, discovery, transport and authentication mechanisms remain implementation-defined. bindings.consumer_context.file identifies consumer-owned contextual input. A Runner MUST NOT interpret its contents as an additional capability grant. How it supplies that context to a model remains implementation-defined. Binding example — the Agent declares @example/review-skill, @example/publish, and a Loop containing draft. This is the value of its bindings object: { "global": { "skills": ["@example/review-skill"] }, "phases": { "draft": { "tools": ["@example/publish"] } } } If the Skill declares a Tool, that Tool is applicable globally. The direct publish Tool is additionally applicable in draft. Cases A–D distinguish applicability, restrictions and invalid phase references. 5. Skills and inherited Tools A Skill packages procedural instructions and supporting resources. Tools supply executable capabilities. Their relationship is a dependency and scope relationship, not an implicit script invocation. APDS-SKILL-001 Skill resources. An author MUST identify the main instructions through skill.entrypoint; supplied complete content MUST contain the declared entrypoint, references and scripts at their safe relative paths. skill.compatibility labels are descriptive compatibility hints. A Runner MUST NOT treat binding a Skill, or finding a script in it, as a command or execution privilege. APDS-SKILL-002 Tool inheritance. A Runner supporting a bound Skill MUST make that Skill's declared Tool dependencies capability candidates in the Skill's binding scope. A global Skill contributes them globally; a phase Skill contributes them only in that phase unless another applicable path contributes them elsewhere. No duplicate direct Tool dependency or binding is required solely for inheritance. Loop restrictions still constrain inherited Tools. APDS-SKILL-003 Repeated paths. Multiple applicable paths to the same resolved Tool MUST preserve its identity and MUST NOT create extra permissions. Each path contributes only within its own scope. A narrower path does not remove a broader independent path. Distinct selected versions MUST NOT be collapsed merely because names match. Internal de-duplication and presentation are implementation choices. Tool execution contracts APDS-TOOL-001 Process invocation. For a Tool process, a compatible Runner MUST supply one input JSON value on stdin that satisfies inputs. A successful invocation requires successful process termination, one JSON value on stdout, and satisfaction of outputs. Non-JSON or log-prefixed stdout and unsuccessful process termination are invocation failures, even if some output looks valid. Diagnostics belong on stderr; diagnostic text alone does not make an otherwise successful invocation fail. A schema-valid application result such as { "ok": false } remains result data if the process succeeds. Host request/result envelopes are not part of the Tool's JSON payload. Runtime services may realize invocation differently while preserving these declared input/output and success distinctions; APDS does not prescribe a host wire protocol or diagnostic codes. The JSON-only output rule describes APDS-conforming Tool execution. An implementation MAY retain an explicitly identified legacy compatibility adapter that accepts historical output, but MUST NOT report that relaxed acceptance as compliance with this strict Tool-output contract. APDS-TOOL-002 Entrypoint and runtime. A Runner interpreting a Tool MUST preserve its declared command, argument order, working-directory meaning and configured timeout. A relative working directory is relative to the Tool's content root. A declared runtime identifies the interpreter family and minimum version; it MUST agree with the declared interpreter. Python runtime.dependencies are distribution requirements, not Component references, and MUST NOT be interpreted as package bindings or Node dependencies. A Runner unable to realize a declared entrypoint setting MUST report that execution limitation rather than silently reinterpret the value. An unavailable interpreter or required runtime service is a readiness failure, not an intrinsic artifact defect. APDS-TOOL-003 Environment precedence. For ordinary Tool variables, a Runner MUST start with ambient environment values, fill absent keys from environment.vars defaults, overlay entrypoint.env, then overlay caller overrides. An existing empty value is present; defaults do not replace it. Required declared variables MUST be present in the resulting invocation environment. Runtime-managed interpreter variables may be reserved by the execution environment; this ordering does not grant permission to override runtime isolation. On non-Tool kinds the root environment field alone introduces no process invocation behavior. 6. Loops and authored orchestration A Loop describes control flow: where execution starts, which phase outcomes exist and where each outcome leads. Array position does not imply execution order. archetype is a descriptive label, not an alternate control-flow algorithm. APDS-LOOP-001 Phases and outcomes. Phase IDs MUST be unique, entry_phase MUST identify a declared phase, and phase objectives MUST contain non-whitespace text. Explicit outcomes MUST have unique IDs within their phase and nonblank descriptions. Omitted outcomes mean exactly one implicit outcome, complete. An explicit outcome list replaces that implicit set; complete is available only if explicitly listed. Runners MUST preserve the outcome identifiers, while choosing their own completion mechanism. APDS-LOOP-002 Deterministic graph. Each transition MUST name a declared source phase, a valid outcome for that source, and a declared destination phase or one of $end, $abort, $handoff. Every valid phase/outcome pair MUST have exactly one transition. All declared phases MUST be reachable from entry_phase through outcome transitions, and at least one terminal MUST be reachable. Branches and cycles MAY occur; this reachability requirement does not assert that every execution terminates. A Runner MUST NOT invent fallback transitions for malformed control flow. APDS-LOOP-003 Terminals. A Runner MUST preserve $end as normal termination, $abort as abort termination and $handoff as yielding control rather than continuing this Loop. It may choose its own result representation and handoff mechanism. APDS-LOOP-004 Step limits. One step is one execution of one Loop phase, including a revisit through a cycle. Tool calls, model turns and Tool retries within that execution are not additional Loop steps. With limits.max_steps present, a Runner MUST NOT begin another phase execution once that many steps have executed. A checkpoint wait or rejected entry does not execute the guarded phase. A Runner may impose stricter operational limits; exhaustion does not authorize exceeding the authored bound or fabricate a successful phase outcome. APDS-LOOP-005 Approval checkpoints. Checkpoint IDs MUST be unique. Each before_phase and on_reject MUST identify a declared phase or, for rejection, a supported terminal. Before entering a guarded phase, a Runner supporting approval checkpoints MUST obtain approval. Multiple checkpoints for that phase apply in authored array order. Approval continues toward phase entry; rejection transfers to on_reject. A pending or unsupported approval MUST NOT be treated as approval. The approval interface and waiting mechanism remain implementation choices. APDS-LOOP-006 Explicit error policy. A Runner supporting the declared policy MUST interpret Tool failure actions as follows: retry permits at most max_retries additional attempts, then applies on_exhausted; fail_phase delegates to the declared phase-failure policy; abort and handoff preserve the corresponding terminal distinction. Retry requires a positive max_retries and on_exhausted; other actions MUST omit both. A policy capable of fail_phase MUST declare phase_failure, whose actions are abort or handoff. Omitted policies leave recovery to the Runner; they do not add an implicit authored retry or transition. Exception classification and backoff remain implementation choices. APDS-LOOP-007 Access policy. A Runner MUST interpret explicit false in phase access.tools or access.knowledge as a prohibition of Tool or Knowledge use, and in access.memory.read/write as a prohibition of direct Agent Memory reads/writes. true permits the corresponding activity under the Loop policy but grants no unbound capability; omission expresses no Loop opinion. Tool restrictions apply to direct, inherited and applicable MCP Tool capabilities. Knowledge permission does not request retrieval, and Memory write permission does not request a write. Separately bound lifecycle operations have the authority described in APDS-MEM-011. Loop example — this complete loop value uses an implicit outcome and an explicit terminal transition: { "entry_phase": "review", "phases": [ { "id": "review", "objective": "Review the supplied evidence.", "access": { "tools": false } } ], "transitions": [{ "from": "review", "on": "complete", "to": "$end" }] } The transition is valid because omitting outcomes supplies complete. An inherited Tool still cannot be used in this phase. See cases B and O. 7. Instruction Profiles A Profile describes intended behavior. It can guide an Agent's identity, priorities and communication without granting capabilities or controlling a Loop's transitions. APDS-PROFILE-001 Authored guidance. A Runner supporting Profiles MUST preserve the distinct meanings of identity (role, description, expertise), objectives and principles (durable priorities), audience (intended readers and adaptation), communication (tone, verbosity, guidelines, formatting and vocabulary), and boundaries (limits on intended behavior or authority). These declarations do not replace the Agent's purpose or a phase's objective. Constraint IDs MUST be unique within a Profile. A Runner MUST preserve the stronger authored obligation of strength: "required" relative to preferred. These are behavioral instructions, not permissions or a guarantee that a model always obeys them. APDS-PROFILE-002 Additive guidance. Global and phase Profiles MUST contribute within their applicable binding scopes under APDS-BIND-003. Repeated references to the same selected Profile MUST preserve its identity and applicability. No precedence follows solely from phase scope, declaration order or prompt placement. Combining Profiles does not define universal natural-language conflict resolution, prompt concatenation order or a de-duplication algorithm. APDS-PROFILE-003 Compatibility expectations. A consumer interpreting compatibility MUST distinguish the author's necessary capability hints in requires from beneficial hints in recommends, and preserve minimum_context_tokens as a context-capacity expectation. A true capability hint asserts that expectation; false or omission does not assert it and is not a prohibition. Hints such as tool_use, structured_output and multimodal_input MUST NOT grant capabilities, override Loop prohibitions or make a conformant Profile invalid merely because the chosen Runner lacks them. Consumers may use them for compatibility decisions or warnings. 8. Knowledge Knowledge supplies authored context or prepared retrieval data. Its metadata describes that content and how it is intended to be used; a declaration alone does not verify its accuracy or trustworthiness. APDS-KNOW-001 Modes and content. Authors and consumers MUST preserve context as direct contextual material and vector as a prepared retrieval corpus with associated embeddings. Context-mode documents identify supplied material; content_type and language describe it, and context holds build-derived aggregate metadata. Vector mode MUST include the schema-required corpus paths and embedding declaration; retrieval indexes remain optional. Chunking metadata describes preparation, not a required query algorithm. A Runner need not inject an entire context corpus into a prompt. APDS-KNOW-002 Packaged relationships. In supplied complete content, declared documents, corpus, vector, index and provenance paths MUST resolve within the artifact. Declared counts and verifiable content relationships MUST agree with their payloads. A validator MUST distinguish checking metadata shape from inspecting actual files. A hash can only be verified when its represented bytes and hash convention are known; APDS does not invent an unspecified aggregate-hash algorithm or file layout from a string label. APDS-KNOW-003 Embeddings and indexes. Consumers MUST preserve embedding identity, provider/model labels, dimensions, metric, normalization state and vector payload association. Declared indexes MUST reference the intended embedding ID; repeated index IDs MUST NOT create an ambiguous association. agentpm-local identifies the schema's supported packaged index type, not a requirement that every Runner implement it. A Runner MUST NOT silently use incompatible embedding or index data as if compatible. Unsupported representation or query-time capabilities are compatibility limits, not proof of artifact nonconformance. APDS-KNOW-004 Retrieval preferences. Consumers interpreting retrieval metadata MUST preserve default_top_k as the default result count, default_score_threshold as a filtering hint and return_citations as the default citation preference. strategy is an open-ended descriptive label, not an implicit algorithm specification. Explicit consumer choices may override defaults. These declarations do not fix ranking, score normalization, citation rendering or an embedding provider. APDS-KNOW-005 Provenance and scope. A consumer MUST distinguish declared sources_manifest_path, generated_at and builder metadata from independently verified provenance. Binding scope and Loop Knowledge restrictions govern availability under APDS-BIND-003 and APDS-LOOP-007. Neither validity nor a binding proves content accuracy, retrieval support or trust. 9. Memory Blueprints, spaces and lifecycle operations A Blueprint describes durable memory, not a live store. Spaces expose logical records; separately bound operations perform lifecycle work under declared inputs, outputs and policies. Record data belongs to runtime state, not the authored Blueprint. APDS-MEM-001 Scopes and record contracts. Space scope keys and record_types MUST refer to declarations in the Blueprint. Their ordered scope tuple identifies the intended logical partition; values come from the consumer. A record type's version identifies its content contract independently of the Blueprint and APDS versions. An operation's space/record-type pair MUST be a declared, permitted pairing, and trigger/delete references MUST identify declared spaces. APDS-MEM-002 Space models. Consumers MUST preserve these logical distinctions: document has one current record for each complete space/scope tuple; collection permits multiple unordered records distinguished by ID; sequence permits multiple ordered records distinguished by ID and ordered by ordinal. A sequence MUST retain monotonically increasing ordinals within that space/scope identity. Physical keys, concurrency and ordinal assignment mechanisms are not fixed. APDS-MEM-003 Retrieval. A document space MUST include key retrieval; a sequence MUST include chronological. A collection needs at least one declared mode. Implementations claiming support MUST preserve key lookup, filter selection, chronological ordering, full_text text retrieval and semantic meaning-based retrieval as distinct capabilities. Unsupported modes MUST be reported as capability limits rather than invalidating the authored Blueprint. No query language, embedding model, ranking algorithm or response API is required. APDS-MEM-004 Capacity, retention and durations. capacity.max_records declares the maximum active-record count within a complete space/scope tuple. A consumer claiming to enforce it MUST preserve that bound rather than silently treating it as a preference. retention.ttl declares active lifetime; after expiration delete removes active availability, while archive removes active retrieval eligibility and permits implementation-specific archival retention. TTL and interval declarations MUST use positive elapsed ISO 8601 durations: a positive integer week component, or positive integer day/hour/minute/second components, with at least one component. Calendar years/months and fractional or zero components are not supported by this contract. Examples are P1W, P7D and PT30M. Cleanup timing, clock storage and archival technology are implementation choices, not new fields or promises of immediate physical erasure. APDS-MEM-005 Append-only. constraints.append_only: true MUST occur only on a collection or sequence. A consumer enforcing it MUST reject ordinary direct update/delete rather than modifying existing records through that surface. Explicit retention and authored lifecycle operations retain their separate mutation authority under APDS-MEM-010; append-only does not prohibit those declared operations. A document space is incompatible with append-only because it defines a current mutable logical document. APDS-MEM-006 Packaged record schemas. A complete Blueprint MUST supply valid Draft 2020-12 JSON Schemas at its declared record-schema paths. Source $ref values MUST remain in-document #... references; they do not authorize arbitrary remote fetching. Applicable record content MUST satisfy its selected record-type schema. A validator inspecting only the manifest MUST leave source-file checks unevaluated. A source schema MUST NOT directly require a property that it marks non-persistable. More complex schema combinations still require evaluation against the actual constraints, not a claim based on a shallow scan. APDS-MEM-007 Operation kinds. A consolidate operation derives output from one or more source pairings; transform converts exactly one source pairing into its declared output; delete targets its declared spaces. Authors MUST preserve their type-specific fields and valid references. A Runner MUST NOT reinterpret these declarations as arbitrary code, Tool bindings or unrestricted CRUD privileges. Record processing techniques remain implementation choices. APDS-MEM-008 Triggers. A Runner interpreting an operation MUST preserve the distinction between its trigger condition and execution: TriggerEligibility meaningexternalRequires an explicit invocation; declaring or binding it does not schedule or execute itintervalRecurring eligibility based on the baseline and successful completion described belowrecord_countAn edge from below the positive threshold to that active scoped count or highercapacityAn edge reaching the named space's declared positive capacity.max_records A capacity trigger MUST identify a space with capacity metadata. For each selected Blueprint operation and resolved scope, count/capacity triggers start armed; an initial observation at or above the threshold satisfies the count condition. Successful execution consumes that edge. A Runner MUST NOT repeatedly fire successful operations merely because an unchanged count remains at or above the threshold; it MUST rearm after observing a count below it. Failure retry policy is separate from rearming. An interval trigger MUST remain dormant until relevant scoped input/target state exists. Its initial baseline starts with that state; first eligibility is baseline plus every. After successful execution, next eligibility is completion time plus every. Re-evaluating a trigger or re-entering a phase MUST NOT itself rearm a consumed edge or reset an established interval baseline. every is a minimum elapsed interval, not a promised execution cadence. Eligibility still requires operation participation in the applicable binding scope and does not guarantee immediate execution, success or backend availability. Polling, yield points, state storage and failure cooldowns remain Runner choices; they must preserve these eligibility guarantees. APDS-MEM-009 Space access and operation participation. A Runner MUST distinguish direct space bindings from operation bindings. Global and phase bindings combine additively for each. A phase-only operation does not participate elsewhere merely because its trigger is eligible. An eligible and authorized operation MAY use its declared inputs, output or target spaces without directly binding those spaces to the Agent. Those operation targets MUST NOT thereby become directly exposed Agent Memory surfaces. An operation-only binding is valid. APDS-MEM-010 Successful output and source handling. A Runner supporting lifecycle operations MUST preserve their declared policies. Successful consolidate/transform completion establishes a valid output under its destination record contract before applying success-dependent source handling. retain keeps sources, retain_until_expiration keeps them under their declared retention, and delete_after_success deletes them only after successful output. Inputs using retain_until_expiration MUST have retention metadata. Transform output_mode defaults to create, producing a new record. replace_input MUST target the same space and record type as its one input and use source_handling: "retain"; it updates that logical record rather than creating another. This is explicit lifecycle authority even on a space that is append-only for direct access, subject to APDS-MEM-011. preserve_provenance: true requires retention of the source relationship in derived output; false does not require that relationship. Delete cascade_derived_records determines whether its intended deletion scope includes derived records. This does not fix transaction engines, retry scheduling or provenance storage. APDS-MEM-011 Direct access and lifecycle operations. Loop access.memory.read and access.memory.write restrictions govern direct Agent access to Memory spaces. A Runner MUST NOT treat those direct-access restrictions as automatically prohibiting separately bound lifecycle operations from accessing their declared inputs, outputs or targets. Operations remain subject to their binding scope, triggers, Blueprint policies, runtime authorization and backend support. An operation MUST NOT make its target spaces directly accessible to the Agent, and no direct binding of every target space is required. APDS-MEM-012 Governance annotations. Record-schema authors MUST use the supported x-agentpm-* names and values; unknown names in that vocabulary are invalid. x-agentpm-data-class categorizes data as public, internal, personal, authentication, financial, health, legal, operational or other. x-agentpm-sensitivity labels severity as low, moderate, high or critical; these classifications alone do not imply access grants or a particular encryption policy. x-agentpm-persist and x-agentpm-shareable are booleans. A consumer claiming support MUST NOT durably persist a value marked x-agentpm-persist: false, or disclose a value marked x-agentpm-shareable: false across Agent, user, tenant, organization, export or synchronization boundaries. A true value does not override other restrictions. These annotations do not certify privacy, legal compliance or security; a consumer unable to honor a restriction must identify that capability limit rather than treating it as permission. APDS-MEM-013 Logical record mapping. A Memory implementation claiming record-contract compatibility MUST be able to map records to the logical envelope below. Physical storage need not use this representation. FieldLogical meaningidNonempty record identifierrecord_type, space, schema_versionThe declared pairing and record-type versionscopeExactly the space's declared keys, with nonempty string valuescreated_atRFC 3339 creation timestampcontentContent satisfying the selected record schemaordinalNonnegative sequence position; required for sequences, absent for other modelsupdated_at, expires_atOptional RFC 3339 update and expiration timestampsprovenanceOptional source-record IDs and declared operation identity Source-record IDs, when supplied, MUST be unique nonempty strings; an operation identity MUST refer to a declared Blueprint operation. Source IDs may survive deletion of the referenced records. Blueprint package/version identity comes from the containing composition or store binding rather than a mandatory repeated envelope field. Operation example — this is a complete transform declaration. Assume declared space notes permits record type note, and summary permits summary: { "type": "transform", "description": "Prepare a summary from a note.", "trigger": { "type": "external" }, "inputs": [{ "space": "notes", "record_type": "note" }], "output": { "space": "summary", "record_type": "summary" }, "source_handling": "retain", "preserve_provenance": true } A phase can bind only this operation, with no direct spaces. Explicit invocation and operation authorization are still required. A prohibition on direct Agent Memory writes does not itself prohibit the operation's declared output write. See cases F, G, L and M. 10. Templates and project scaffolding A Template describes a generated project. The Template, that project and its referenced Agents or Components keep separate identities. APDS-TEMPLATE-001 Files and variables. files_root MUST identify the safe artifact-relative directory supplying scaffold content. A compatible instantiator MUST preserve the intended files and declared {{ variable_name }} substitutions without allowing paths to escape their permitted roots. Variable names MUST be unique. Explicit generation values override defaults; unresolved required variables or declared placeholders needed by the generated content MUST NOT be silently treated as successfully resolved. Unrelated content is not a substitution instruction. Variables are non-secret configuration, not fields for publishing runtime credentials. Prompting, destination naming, copying and overwrite interfaces are implementation choices. APDS-TEMPLATE-002 Dependencies and entrypoints. A consumer MUST preserve the identities, kinds and version constraints in Template dependency groups. They describe the generated workspace's intended composition. entrypoints label suggested commands for that project; declaring or instantiating a Template MUST NOT itself be interpreted as authorization to execute them. Successful generation does not establish successful installation or command execution. APDS-TEMPLATE-003 Execution surfaces. A consumer interpreting an execution-surface identifier MUST preserve its authored target: IdentifierIntended integrationpython-sdkA Python SDK consumer applicationnode-sdkA Node SDK consumer applicationagentpm-runDirect Tool invocation through AgentPMagentpm-harnessAgent execution through AgentPM's built-in Runneragentpm-serve-mcpServing Tool capabilities over MCP through AgentPMmulti-agent-workspaceA workspace composing multiple Agents display_name and use_case describe purpose; stack labels project technologies. These are compatibility intentions, not evidence that dependencies, services, credentials or runtime support exist. Supporting APDS does not oblige an implementation to provide every listed integration or a particular generation command. 11. Conformance, interpretation and compatibility Conformance concerns an artifact and its applicable authored relationships. A validation result records what one evaluation established from the supplied context. These are related but different claims. APDS-CONF-001 Evaluation scopes. Validators MUST identify which applicable requirements they evaluated: ScopeAvailable evidenceStandalone (intrinsic)The manifest's shape and local semantic relationshipsResolved-compositionSelected dependency manifests and their cross-artifact relationshipsPackaged-contentReferenced files or generated artifacts supplied for inspection Runner interpretation checks establish observable behavior for supported constructs; they are not a requirement that a manifest validator execute Tools, lifecycle operations, model calls or a Runner. Passing one scope MUST NOT be presented as passing another unevaluated scope. APDS-CONF-002 Absent context versus absent content. A validator MUST distinguish unavailable dependencies/files from definite authored defects. Requirements needing unavailable inspection context remain unevaluated. When an otherwise complete supplied artifact lacks required content, or an available graph establishes an invalid reference, the corresponding requirement is violated. A definite violation remains a violation even if other checks are unevaluated. APDS-CONF-003 Logical outcomes. An implementation MUST preserve these distinctions in its claims: OutcomeMeaningConformant within a stated scopeAll applicable requirements in that completed scope were satisfiedNonconformantAt least one definite applicable violation was establishedIncomplete / not fully evaluatedNeeded evidence is unavailable, so remaining requirements cannot be decidedUnsupportedThe declared standard/version, evaluation scope or interpretation capability is not supported Unsupported or incomplete evaluation MUST NOT masquerade as successful verification or, by itself, as a definite semantic violation. A supported declaration alone establishes no conformance. Implementations may support several versions, but MUST interpret each using its declared contract, not substitute another version. APDS-CONF-004 Independent evidence. A consumer MUST distinguish artifact conformance, distribution trust, Runner compatibility and local execution readiness. Signatures, attestations and scanning provide their own evidence; publication or installation alone does not prove APDS conformance. Missing credentials, services or a supported backend do not retroactively invalidate an otherwise conformant artifact. APDS-CONF-005 Truthful reporting. Implementations MUST limit support and verification claims to their actual roles, capabilities and completed checks. Findings SHOULD identify the standard version, evaluated scope, affected declaration and stable rule ID so a developer can locate the requirement. APDS does not require a particular enum, API result shape, error wording, UI, certification service or internal validator architecture. Missing-standard compatibility interpretations MUST remain distinguishable from explicit APDS 1.0.0 conformance and MUST NOT fabricate historical validation evidence.Read the frozen semantics.md source. This reference describes definitions and interpretation; it is not evidence of a package’s runtime readiness, safety or quality.
